item.title: Rising Appalachia: Hurricane Helene Anniversary Shows — Sun Sep 27 — Pisgah Brewing Company Black Mountain
item.description:
Sunday, September 27 | Doors: 2 pm | Show: 3 pm | From $40.83 adv. Event Details & Tickets
Rising AppalachiaIn Appalachia, farmers still practice the ancestral tradition of companion planting. Corn grows tall as a trellis, beans climb the corn, and squash provides the ground cover. Rising Appalachia cultivates a similar symbiosis in their music, where Southern folk traditions, New Orleans swamp culture, and Atlanta’s street spirit strengthen each other. Known for their seamless harmonies, songcatching and storytelling, the band has released ten albums and toured throughout North America, South America, Europe, the Celtic Isles, Australia and beyond — performing everywhere from the Telluride Bluegrass Festival and Red Rocks to NPR’s Tiny Desk. All the while, the band has cultivated a devoted grassroots following traveling to communities big and small by train, horseback, bio-diesel bus and sailboat.

item.title: Sam's Gap to Big Bald; 13.0 miles. Fitness Hike. — Wed Sep 30, 9:30 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group **TYPE OF HIKE:** Out & Back **DISTANCE:** 13.0 miles **ELEVATION GAIN:** approximately 3,250'
HIKE DESCRIPTION: Let’s enjoy one of the last few warm days of the season!!
This is a beautiful and challenging (level 10) roller-coaster style fitness hike on a well-maintained trail that trecks over several ridge lines to the Summit of Big Bald Mountain & back. This includes an initial climb to a grassy meadow from which one can see the summit of Big Bald, (the tallest peak centered in the picture). This trail then continues an up-and-down course along the NC and TN boundaries. There are at least 1 or 2 small springs that may be active at this time of the year. The summit is an open bald where we will break for a snack and enjoy the views before returning. The hike is mostly under a hardwood canopy until the summit. On the summit, the higher elevation temperatures are about 10 degrees cooler than Asheville's weather and often breezy.

item.title: Craven Gap North Out-and-Back -- 5.6 mi, 850 ft. elev. gain — Fri Oct 2, 9:00 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group **[Sign-ups open Sunday, September 27th, 8:00 PM]**
Those who attended last week's hike will recognize the trailhead. But this time we'll hike north rather than south.
This segment of the Mountain-to-Sea Trail was devastated by Hurricane Helene and closed for well over a year. But it's back! If you're familiar with this hike, you'll find it was radically altered, changing from mostly shady to mostly sunny with some new vistas along the way.
This hilly trek goes north on the Mountain-to-Sea Trail from the Craven Gap Parking lot. You should have experience on comparable or more strenuous hikes so you won't hold up the group. We'll go out and back, about 2.8 miles each way with a 15-minute break in the middle. Our pace will be around 2.4 mph. We should return to the parking lot soon after noon.
**Dogs:** Well-behaved dogs are welcome, but Forestry Service regulations require leashes.

item.title: Lea and Heffernan of Wheelchair Sports Camp — Fri Oct 9, 3:00 PM
item.description:
Gaelynn Lea and Kalyn Rose Heffernan of Wheelchair Sports Camp will visit UNC Asheville for an afternoon talk and evening performance. At 3 p.m., Lea and Heffernan will discuss disability culture, access, and activism, sharing their experiences as artists and advocates working to make the arts more inclusive. At 6 p.m., Wheelchair Sports Camp will take the stage for a free performance. Lea, winner of NPR Music’s Tiny Desk Contest, is an accomplished violinist, songwriter, composer, and disability advocate who has performed around the world and composed the score for Macbeth on Broadway. Wheelchair Sports Camp, led by wheelchair-using rapper Kalyn Rose Heffernan, blends hip-hop, humor, and high-energy performance. The Denver-based band has expanded its work beyond music into performance art, museums, theater, film, and activism. Both events are free and open to the public and will take place in the Blue Ridge Room of the Highsmith Student Union.

item.title: Queen Bee and the Honeylovers — Fri Oct 16, 7:00 PM — Meadow at Highland Brewing Co.
item.description:
Sweet, sweet Swing
Queen Bee and the Honeylovers are rooted in the jazz and blues of the 1930’s and 40’s. Their original compositions nod to these classic styles with lyrical content that explores modern themes that feel both timeless and immediate. Their debut album, ‘Asheville’, celebrated their hometown’s history and won them #41 on WNCW’s listener-voted poll of Best Albums of 2019 as well as features on The State of Things with Frank Stasio and PBS Woodsongs. Their video for “Beacham’s Curve” won Best Soundtrack at the 2019 Music Video Asheville Awards. The Honeylovers approach early jazz not as a static genre but as a living language. Their work reflects an ongoing dialogue between past and present, using the forms of early American music to explore contemporary questions of place, identity, and cultural memory. item.title: Guided Trail Walk — Sat Oct 17, 10:00 AM
item.description: Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center.

item.title: See the Sights of Cherokee on a 10 KM/6.2 mile Walk — Sat Nov 21, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group We'll gather at the Welcome Center across from the fairgrounds. Our route takes us past the Museum of the Cherokee People and the Qualla Arts and Crafts facility. We then walk the road up to the *Unto These Hills* Amphitheatre. From there we pass the Oconaluftee Indian Village and walk through the Botanical Gardens. Coming back down the back way, we loop around ending up at the Oconaluftee Islands Park with its "bamboo forest." From there we return to the start point.
Hiking boots are not needed, though some will want walking poles. (I plan to take both of mine.) Do bring plenty of water and a protein snack. Dress for the weather. I'm not sure whether dogs are allowed in the Botanical Gardens, but it is a short loop and if necessary, you can walk around the parking lot for the few minutes it will take us to make that loop. While much of this walk is on pavement, trail strollers would be needed for the walk, with a few workarounds.
